ELI5: Why do people keep buying brand name items when store brand items are so much cheaper?

Sometimes brand name is just better. Sometimes it is not. I know for some of my favorites, it is about the consistency of the food, that makes a huge difference.

Besides that, marketing and packaging are a big deal for a reason, people still eat that shit up. If they didn't, we wouldn't see ads literally everywhere.

It's partly about the security of the familiar, and secondly about the perceived quality and status associated with the more expensive, brand named product.

Familiarity is more typically associated with essential goods: I've tried these foodstuffs before, I've seen them advertised, I know what to expect from them, I'll buy some.

Status, as is probably quite obvious, is more associated with want purchases; items you don't need to survive, but want any way because you have convinced yourself that certain benefits will manifest themselves after the sale, in order to justify the higher price: my friends will be so jealous; now everyone will see how sophisticated and well off I am.

I am way over simplifying things of course, but that's my contribution to this topic.
